items.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025
items.q: The interviewee responds to the interviewer's mention of Louis Hayes by discussing general drumming styles and other drummers (Paul Chambers, Elvin Jones, Tony Williams), but does not mention playing with, meeting, or having a personal relationship with Louis Hayes.

ctx.x: more than that hi-hat two and four. You know. So I’m listening for that. And that lets me know if I’m in sync with his quarter note, if I’m a little behind I’m a little bit – and every drummer’s different. You know I play with guys that really are on top of the beat and you’ve really gotta push. And then you get used to playing with a guy like that, then you’re playing with someone that plays a little behind the beat and you’re pushing him and you don’t want to push him. You know? You want to relax and breathe.…

I remember hearing Louis Hayes and I think it was Ron Carter on bass at the Iridium. This was quite a few years ago. And Louis Hayes was so on top of the beat that I couldn’t understand how the song did not speed up like significantly. How is that possible? Man he just like constant push yet not speeding up I guess.

Yeah well you know some people have set it up as a big circle you know. So you could be a little bit ahead you know, or you could be a little behind. We could be right in the middle. I always kind of felt Paul Chambers and that group of Miles Davis were kind of right on the beat you know. And when you listen to Elvin Jones and Jimmy Garrison I always felt they were just a little behind. They left more room for Elvin’s big circular triplety things that he did. And when you listen to Ron Carter and Tony Williams…
